clue.text: Large cat doesn't finish eating large fruit

indicators.note: a word that does not finish loses its final letter
something eating another thing holds it inside its body

blocks.note: the puma is a big American wild cat
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A big cat, interrupted mid-meal, leaves a huge piece of fruit half eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: PUMA cut short is PUM, which wraps round L to make PLUM. Professor Plum is one of the suspects in the board game Clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A plum is a stone fruit, so the general word names one example of it.

clue.text: Candidate spraying "gay fog" is a follower of Joseph Smith, possibly

definitions.text: a follower of Joseph Smith, possibly

indicators.note: spraying scatters things about, so the letters of the quoted word are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: pol is American slang for a politician, here one standing for office
the word itself, to be rearranged
mist is a thin fog

explanation.surface: A political candidate sprays a slogan about fog, and someone wonders whether this makes them a Mormon.
explanation.walkthrough: Joseph Smith founded the Latter Day Saint movement and took many wives; plural marriage was practised by early Mormons, hence the hedge 'possibly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Early Mormon doctrine endorsed plural marriage, so a polygamist could well be one of Smith's adherents.

clue.text: Tradition in our time?

blocks.note: 'our' belongs to us
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A question about whether old customs survive in the present day.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is established custom or practice, a near synonym of tradition.

clue.text: Someone, moving in the old ways, ran and flocked together in disarray

definitions.text: Someone, moving in the old ways

indicators.note: things in disarray are thrown out of order, so these letters must be put into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in old habits runs and joins a disorderly crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving in the old ways' reads like being old-fashioned, but it describes stepping to traditional dances.
explanation.definitionFit: A folk dancer performs traditional dances, literally moving in the time-honoured fashion.

clue.text: Freeway entrance with Ronald and Pamela each shifting front to back

indicators.note: each name moves its opening letter to its end, a rotation of the word

blocks.note: Ron is the short form of Ronald
Pam is the short form of Pamela

explanation.surface: Two people named Ronald and Pamela change places at a highway junction.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pet names rotate their first letter to the back before joining.
explanation.definitionFit: An on-ramp is the American term for the slip road leading onto a motorway.

clue.text: Extremely truculent in military headgear, the writer clapped hands, maybe

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two end letters
one piece sits in another, enclosed by it

blocks.note: the first and last letters of the word
a kepi is a flat-topped French military cap
the writer of the clue refers to themselves

explanation.surface: A belligerent soldier in a cap, and the author applauding.
explanation.walkthrough: A kepi is the flat-topped cap of French soldiers and police; 'clapped hands' is only one way of marking the beat.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping time means marking the beat of music, and clapping along is one way of doing it.

clue.text: A bishop remains? For shame!

blocks.note: taken as written
B is the chess notation for a bishop
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A scandalised exclamation about a bishop's leftover belongings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For shame!' looks like a set phrase, but only 'shame' is the definition, as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To abash someone is to make them embarrassed or ashamed, so it works as the verb sense of shame.

clue.text: Two companies, smuggling heroin, delayed an addictive substance?

indicators.note: to smuggle something is to carry it hidden inside

blocks.note: CO, the abbreviation for company, twice
H is drug slang for heroin
something delayed arrives late

explanation.surface: A tale of two firms running heroin, with the drug shipment held up.
explanation.walkthrough: The H goes inside the first CO. The question mark flags the joke that the 'addictive substance' is only a sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Chocolate is jokingly called addictive by those who crave it, hence the playful question mark.

clue.text: Libertine's inclination

blocks.note: first meaning: a dissolute man about town
second meaning: the slope or angle of a surface, such as a stage

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a libertine's tendencies; 'inclination' is really a physical slant.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a debauched man and the angle of tilt of a stage or a ship's mast.

clue.text: Business leader and I reread Lean In every other year

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
rereading the title here means reading its letters in a fresh arrangement

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
taken as written
the book title, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A business executive and the speaker revisit Sheryl Sandberg's book every two years.
explanation.walkthrough: Lean In is Sheryl Sandberg's 2013 book on women in business, which makes 'Business leader' look like a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Biennial means occurring once in two years, at intervals of every second year.

clue.text: More lush? That's a relief, surprisingly

indicators.note: an unexpected outcome hints that the letters land in an unexpected order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether more drink is on offer and is unexpectedly relieved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lush' suggests a drunk and 'That's a relief' a sigh, but lush here means thickly green.
explanation.definitionFit: Lush vegetation is dense and full of foliage, so a plant with more leaves looks lusher.

clue.text: Texas city, lacking leadership, invested in Gregory's bird

indicators.note: without its leader the word loses its first letter
something invested in another is put inside it

blocks.note: Waco is a city in central Texas
Gregory Peck, the Hollywood actor

explanation.surface: A beheaded Texan town put into an actor's pet bird, as if it were money in a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gregory's bird' looks like a pet, but the possessive just points to the actor Gregory Peck. Mrs Peacock is one of the suspects in Clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The peacock is the male peafowl, a large bird with a showy fanned tail.

clue.text: Environmentally sound generators, halfbroken

indicators.note: run together as one word, it says only half of the word survives and that half is smashed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, before halving

explanation.surface: Eco-friendly power generators, only half working.
explanation.walkthrough: The front half GENER is rearranged. Reverend Green is the Clue suspect called Mr Green in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Green describes anything friendly to the environment, a common political and commercial sense.

clue.text: Competition fight in a ring — this has what it takes to set you on fire

definitions.text: this has what it takes to set you on fire

blocks.note: a match is a sporting contest
boxers fight in a ring

explanation.surface: A boxing bout described as a fiery, inspiring contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set you on fire' sounds like rousing excitement, but it is literal: a matchbox holds the means of lighting a flame.
explanation.definitionFit: A matchbox contains matches, which are exactly the means needed to start a fire.

clue.text: Tamper with grown-up's online fee?

blocks.note: an adult is a grown-up
an e-rate, a charge made over the internet

explanation.surface: Someone meddles with a grown-up's internet charges.
explanation.definitionFit: To adulterate is to tamper with something by mixing in inferior ingredients.

clue.text: Artwork of a biblical prophet

blocks.note: first meaning: a picture made of small tiles or pieces of glass
second meaning: relating to Moses, as in the law he handed down

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a painting of a prophet, but the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names a tiled picture, and the adjective, from Moses, describes things associated with that lawgiver.

clue.text: They entrust gestation to the male, so shes are running wild

definitions.text: They entrust gestation to the male

indicators.note: running wild means out of control, so these letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: With the fathers carrying the babies, the mothers are free to go out on the town.
explanation.definitionFit: Among seahorses the male carries the eggs in a brood pouch until they hatch.

clue.text: Darn tot tipped over a condiment

indicators.note: something tipped over ends up the other way round, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: both are mild curses
to tot up is to add, giving a sum

explanation.surface: A parent curses as a toddler knocks over the sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tot' looks like a toddler but means a total. Colonel Mustard is one of the Clue suspects.
explanation.definitionFit: Mustard is a pungent yellow paste served as a condiment with meats.

clue.text: Bad wine interrupts goalie's accomplishment in curve

indicators.note: bad wine is spoiled, so its letters are spoiled into another order
to interrupt is to break into the middle of something

blocks.note: taken as written
a goalkeeper's job is to make a save

explanation.surface: A goalkeeper's great stop is spoiled by cheap wine, ending up in a bend in the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A sine wave is the smooth repeating graph of the sine function, the standard oscillating curve.

clue.text: Secure '60s band? What a treat!

blocks.note: in American sports slang, to ice a game is to secure the win
Cream was Eric Clapton's 1960s rock trio

explanation.surface: Getting hold of a beloved sixties group is called a real treat.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs from 19-across into the down light that says 'See 19'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice cream is the classic frozen dessert people reward themselves with, the archetypal treat.

clue.text: Repeated letters from cadet are tiresome during a recession

indicators.note: the answer is made of consecutive letters taken from the phrase that follows
a recession is a going back, so those letters are read backwards

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the three words

explanation.surface: A cadet's repetitive chants grow wearisome in an economic slump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recession' looks economic but signals reading backwards; the letters sit across caDET ARE TIresome.
explanation.definitionFit: Iterated means said or done again, a direct synonym of repeated.

clue.text: Red small mark?

blocks.note: a scar is a mark left by a wound
-let is a suffix making things small, as in booklet

explanation.surface: A small red spot on the skin.
explanation.walkthrough: Read SCAR + LET as a 'small scar', which is how the question mark plays it. Miss Scarlet is one of the Clue suspects.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet is a vivid shade of red.

clue.text: Ailing source for international water?

blocks.note: the UN is the international body of nations
a well is where water comes from

explanation.surface: An unhealthy supply of drinking water for global use.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads as a well belonging to the UN.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwell means sick or in poor health, a close synonym for ailing.

clue.text: Reflect more paltry broadcast

indicators.note: what is broadcast reaches listeners by ear, so the spoken form counts

blocks.note: merer, the comparative of mere, means more insignificant

explanation.surface: A radio station broadcasting even meaner content asks itself to think.
explanation.walkthrough: MERER is a rarely seen comparative of mere, but valid.
explanation.definitionFit: To mirror is to reflect, as a surface throws back an image.

clue.text: Enchant Circe (not with musical works)

indicators.note: an enchantment transforms its victim, so these letters are transformed into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the name as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A request to charm the sorceress of the Odyssey without using any music.
explanation.walkthrough: Circe, who turned Odysseus's men into pigs, is the right victim for an enchanting transformation. The parentheses pretend 'not with' means without; it is fodder plus link.
explanation.definitionFit: Concerti is the Italian plural of concerto, a composition for soloist and orchestra.

clue.text: See 19
Joshua and Henri taking in a successful movie like Milk

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it inside

blocks.note: the puzzle's two setters, speaking of themselves
a hit is a box-office success

explanation.surface: The setters go to see a successful film resembling Gus Van Sant's Milk.
explanation.walkthrough: Milk is the 2008 Harvey Milk biopic, which makes the definition look like a film comparison. Mrs White is one of the Clue suspects.
explanation.definitionFit: Milk is the standard example of something white in colour.

clue.text: Report studied fish model

indicators.note: a report is something spoken, so the phrase is heard rather than read

blocks.note: eyed means studied, and an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: An account of someone examining a fish-shaped model.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideal is a perfect example to follow, as a model is.

clue.text: Republican's No. 2 commitment in connection with a party

definitions.text: commitment in connection with a party

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for Republican
the S of the possessive
the vice president is second in command

explanation.surface: A Republican running mate makes a pledge on behalf of his party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' looks political, but it is a social gathering you answer an invitation to.
explanation.definitionFit: Replying RSVP to an invitation commits a guest to attending, or not, a social party.

clue.text: Distrust head of school mishandling PE cuts

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
handling things wrongly muddles them, so the letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Staff distrust a headteacher who bungles cuts to gym classes.
explanation.walkthrough: PE is physical education. This is the 28 of the puzzle's theme: Clue's six suspects all appear in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspect someone is to mistrust them or believe them guilty.

clue.text: Wandering, I arrive in coastal region

indicators.note: wandering means straying from a set path, so these letters stray from their order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A traveller roams until reaching a stretch of seaside.
explanation.definitionFit: A riviera is a coastal resort area, after the famous Mediterranean stretch in France and Italy.

clue.text: Modest revision in writing that is lewd and deconstructive, perhaps?

indicators.note: a revision reworks a text, so these letters are reworked into a new order
one piece is placed in the other

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
pornography is lewd writing

explanation.surface: A literary critic describes a bawdy text that has been tamed by editing.
explanation.walkthrough: Deconstruction is the literary theory of Derrida, a hallmark of postmodern thought, hence 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Deconstructive criticism is one example of the postmodern approach to texts and meaning.

clue.text: Oddly, culture produces a game involving the six 28s that appear in the grid

definitions.text: a game involving the six 28s that appear in the grid

indicators.note: taking the word oddly keeps its first, third, fifth and seventh letters

blocks.note: the odd-numbered letters of the word

explanation.surface: A quirky civilisation invents a game featuring the puzzle's hidden characters.
explanation.walkthrough: Clue, called Cluedo in Britain, has six suspects: Plum, Peacock, Green, Mustard, Scarlet and White, all in this grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Clue is the murder-mystery board game whose players deduce which of six suspects did it.
